core_obligations: The inequality (proof lines 2812-2828): since the underlying spaces are irreducible and sober the dominance of f means that the generic point of X maps to the generic point of Y; the dimension formula for algebraic spaces bounds the dimension of the local ring of X at any point by the dimension at its image plus the transcendence degree, and dimensions are suprema of the dimensions of the local rings, which gives the inequality.

Reduction to the quasi-compact case (proof lines 2830-2840): if the equality holds over each nonempty quasi-compact open of Y then it holds for X over Y, so one may assume both spaces quasi-compact; a locally Noetherian decent algebraic space is quasi-separated, so there is a finite surjective morphism from a scheme onto Y, which may be chosen integral.

Reduce to schemes (proof lines 2840-2870): choosing an integral closed subspace of the fibre product finite and surjective over X and then a finite surjective morphism from an integral scheme onto it gives a commutative square of integral spaces with X'' and Y' schemes finite and surjective over X and Y; dimension is unchanged under such morphisms, the generic points map to the generic points with finite residue field extensions, so the transcendence degree is unchanged, and the equality follows from the case of schemes.
proof_roadmap: Read the inequality off from the pointwise dimension formula and the description of dimension as a supremum.
In the proper case reduce to a quasi-compact situation and produce finite surjective schemes over the two spaces.
Compare dimensions and transcendence degrees across the finite surjective maps and invoke the scheme case of the formula.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a dominant locally of finite type morphism of integral algebraic spaces over a locally Noetherian base, the dimension of the source is at most the dimension of the target plus the transcendence degree of the extension of residue fields at the generic points, with equality when the morphism is proper (statement lines 2810-2825). The proof (proof lines 2827-2887) derives the inequality from the pointwise dimension formula, and in the proper case reduces to a quasi-compact situation, produces finite surjective integral schemes over both spaces, and compares dimensions and transcendence degrees to invoke the case of schemes. H3: a reduction to the scheme case with a genuine comparison of dimensions and transcendence degrees, written out in full.
